# Summary {#part-generative-summary .unnumbered}

This part set aside the left-to-right text spine and studied generation for objects that are not naturally token sequences. Diffusion, flow matching, non-autoregressive language modeling, speech, image generation, video, world models, and robotics all depend on an order that the system constructs over its output so that learning, sampling, caching, and evaluation become possible.

Each constructed order has costs. A representation that helps training may make serving harder, higher sampling fidelity often multiplies latency, and a multimodal fusion scheme can obscure where the evidence came from. The recurring question across the part was therefore what it costs to translate a physical or perceptual object into a representation a model can process.

The part leaves open whether grounded experience and robotics data can scale with anything like the regularity of text. If they cannot, the bottleneck will move from model design to the collection, reuse, and verification of physical-world data. Part III returns to behavior: once a model can generate through these orders, the next question is which behaviors should be encouraged, refused, ranked, or corrected.
